inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense FY2025 $175M (3.2% of revenue; above the $163M cash-flow add-back, used as the more complete figure); FY2026E $190M = 3.1% of guided revenue (H1-26 cash-flow add-back $94M). Net-share-settlement withholding taxes are not tagged in XBRL after FY2021 (FY2019-21 ran $28-48M/yr) and are NOT separately added -- house SBC may understate the true cost by up to ~$30M/yr.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 47.31M basic on the 10-Q cover (2026-07-28) + 0.41M dilutive securities (Q2-26 diluted 48.13M less basic 47.72M weighted). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed. Zebra is an active repurchaser ($587M FY25, $568M H1-26), so the flat count is funded, not a convention.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Rf 4.3% (10y UST) + beta ~1.3 x ERP 5.0% = CoE ~10.8%; debt ~15% of EV at ~4.5% after tax -> WACC ~9.9%, rounded to 10.0%. Same WACC in every scenario: cyclicality is charged once, in the bear flows and the 25% bear weight, not in a rate premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842: operating lease cost is already inside opex/adjusted EBITDA (treatment B by construction); operating lease liabilities ($194M at 2026-07-04) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt. lease_cost_pct_path = 0.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component route) with the cyclical adaptations -- Zebra is a US operating company selling rugged enterprise hardware (mobile computers, scanners, printers, RFID, machine vision) whose demand follows enterprise capex/refresh cycles (FY22->FY23 revenue -21%, owner FCF negative in FY23). Base case therefore glides margins back to a mid-cycle adjusted-EBITDA margin (22.5%) rather than capitalising the FY26 up-cycle peak (23.5-24.0% guided). FY0 is FY2026E built from the Q2-26 raised guidance (sales +14-16% incl. Elo Touch, acquired Q4-25 for ~$1.3B; adj. EBITDA margin 23.5-24.0%; FCF >$1.0B); base_revenue = FY25 $5,396M x 1.15. Year 1 = FY2027. Net debt is the 2026-07-04 balance sheet (debt $2,776M incl. $2,275M now current -- a refinancing event, not a solvency one at ~2x EBITDA; cash $157M); H2-26 FCF is assumed to be consumed by the ongoing buyback, so no cash build is credited. last_fcf = guided FY26 FCF $1,000M - SBC $190M (levered, after ~$140M interest); the engine itself builds UNLEVERED owner FCF from EBITDA and deducts net debt once in the bridge, so interest is not double-counted. The ~$73M IEEPA tariff refund claim is excluded (contingent, one-off). Interest income is 0: the company is net-debt. EBITDA basis: adjusted EBITDA (pre-SBC); SBC charged as its own line.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Revenue 5yr CAGR (3.9%) cross-checked against management's 5-7% organic sales CAGR target; equity CAGR rejected (see warning)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (10.9% 5yr) diverges >30% from revenue (3.9%) and EPS (-2.7%) CAGRs. Book value grew on retained earnings and the 2025 Elo acquisition, while FY20->FY25 EPS fell across a full destock cycle; equity CAGR is not a usable growth proxy for a cyclical repurchaser.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC): FY20 $836M, FY22 $317M, FY25 $656M. The 3yr figure starts at the FY22 trough and is not a growth rate; the 5yr owner-FCF CAGR (-4.7%) is below reported (-1.5%) because SBC rose from $59M to $175M (1.3% -> 3.2% of revenue) -- an increasing share of reported cash flow is being paid in stock. All endpoints are FY2020/FY2022/FY2025 annual rows of ZBRA_Metrics.csv.

base.narrative: Refresh cycle and Elo integration carry FY27 to +6%, then growth settles into management's 5-7% organic band and fades to 3%. Adjusted EBITDA margin gives back the FY26 tariff-mitigation and volume-leverage peak to a 22.5% mid-cycle level (FY21 23.4%, FY23 trough ~18%, FY24-25 ~21.5%).

bull.narrative: Machine vision, RFID mandates and Frontline AI software scale into a real mix shift: growth runs at the top of the 5-7% organic target plus Elo, the post-pandemic installed base refreshes on schedule, and higher-margin software/recurring revenue lifts adjusted EBITDA to 25.5% with tariff mitigation complete.

bear.narrative: FY26 proves to be a pull-forward: channel partners (ScanSource, BlueStar, Ingram ~50% of sales) destock as in FY22-23, revenue falls 10% in FY27, renewed tariffs and low-cost Asian scanners cap the recovery, and adjusted EBITDA margin settles at 21% while smartphone/computer-vision capture slowly erodes dedicated-device demand.

scenario_narratives.base: Refresh cycle and Elo integration carry FY27 to +6%, then growth settles into management's 5-7% organic band and fades to 3% by FY34. Adjusted EBITDA margin returns from the FY26 guided 23.75% peak to a 22.5% mid-cycle level as tariff tailwinds and volume leverage normalise. SBC 3.1% of revenue gliding to 2.6%; cash tax ramps 20% -> 21%.
scenario_narratives.bull: Machine vision (Photoneo, Matrox), RFID tagging mandates and the Frontline AI Suite turn Zebra into a software-enabled automation platform: growth 9% fading to 3.5%, adjusted EBITDA 25.5% on software mix and completed tariff mitigation, exit multiple 16x owner FCF.
scenario_narratives.bear: The FY26 beat is a channel pull-forward: distributors destock as in FY22-23 (revenue -21% then), FY27 revenue -10% with adjusted EBITDA margin at 19%, recovering only to 21% as tariffs return and low-cost Asian entrants and smartphone/vision-based capture press on pricing; 12x exit.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: Zebra is a high-cyclicality hardware name priced near its 52-week high after a ~30% re-rate on one beat-and-raise quarter, with ~50% of sales through three distributors that destocked hard in FY22-23. Base 50% as the mid-cycle path consistent with management's 5-7% organic target. Bull trimmed to 25% because it needs several independent things (software/vision mix shift, RFID adoption, durable tariff relief) to all go right.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Cyclical enterprise-hardware compounder valued on unlevered owner FCF (SBC fully expensed, share count flat) through a mid-cycle margin lens: the FY26 guided peak is the starting point, not the run-rate. Cyclicality is charged in the bear flows and weight, not in the discount rate.
key_risks_to_valuation: Channel destock: ~50% of sales via ScanSource, BlueStar and Ingram Micro; FY22-23 showed a -21% revenue swing
Peak-margin extrapolation: FY26 adjusted EBITDA 23.5-24.0% includes tariff-mitigation and volume leverage that may not persist
Refinancing: $2,275M of debt is current at 2026-07-04
Tariff regime changes; the ~$73M IEEPA refund is excluded
Equity-award withholding taxes not disclosed in XBRL after FY2021, so house SBC may be understated by up to ~$30M/yr
